newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eurorand bond issues boom with foreign investors buying about 850 million rand of bonds since the start of the year to cash in on South Africa's high interest rates.
- South Africa's information technology group Persetel Holdings Ltd said it will buy a 70 percent controlling stake in the German company Telemation AG for an undisclosed sum.

- The Appellate Division has protected a U.S. firm from infringement of its trademark rights in South Africa. Luster Products, which manufactures black hair products, has won exclusive rights to their trademark "S Curl" hair relaxants.
- Local bonds benefit from Eurorands as five launches help revive interest in South Africa.

- New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) deputy executive chairman Cyril Ramaphosa denies that the black consortium is interested in plans to have black investors taken on board as shareholders of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, the country's second largest gold producer
- KwaZulu-Natal province mulls regional stock exchange as a leg-up to small business and accelerate economic growth.
- Republic Ratings enters into joint venture with U.S.-based international rating agency Duff and Phelps Credit Rating Co.
- South Africa's justice and police ministers meet to push for law leading to tougher bail conditions for serious crimes, amid mounting public anger over cases of violent crime.
- President Mandela admits the ANC has made fundamental mistakes in its first half-term in office and calls for a people-centred Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP).
